name: Mobile Location Data
title: Mobile Location Data
answer: Mobile location data is the record of where a phone or tablet has been, inferred from GPS, Wi-Fi, cell tower and beacon signals. In alternative data it is used as a proxy for foot traffic, store visits, commuting patterns and catchment areas. It covers both raw pings and derived measures such as visit counts, dwell time and trade area overlap. The data is usually sold as aggregated panels or as scores rather than as individual trails. It sits alongside card transactions, web traffic and satellite imagery in the alternative data stack.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Mobile location data is the record of where a phone or tablet has been, inferred from GPS, Wi-Fi, cell tower and beacon signals. In alternative data it is used as a proxy for foot traffic, store visits, commuting patterns and catchment areas. It covers both raw pings and derived measures such as visit counts, dwell time and trade area overlap. The data is usually sold as aggregated panels or as scores rather than as individual trails. It sits alongside card transactions, web traffic and satellite imagery in the alternative data stack.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on the handset first, where operating systems and app software development kits collect location signals under platform permissions. Those signals travel through app backends, advertising exchanges and location data brokers to cloud storage and processing pipelines. Processing typically uses distributed systems for stream ingestion, geospatial indexing and time series storage. Analysts then query the results through business intelligence tools, notebooks or mapping platforms. The infrastructure must handle high volume, uneven sampling and frequent changes in device settings.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The method starts with consent and collection rules, then filters pings for accuracy, speed and impossible jumps. Engineers snap coordinates to road networks or building footprints, build visit events with dwell thresholds and assign them to points of interest. They weight panels to match known population totals and aggregate to protect individuals. Common outputs include foot traffic indices, trade area maps and co-location measures. Validation compares the panel against ground truth such as store counts or traffic counters.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk turn on consent, purpose limitation, retention and the line between anonymous and identifiable data. Mobile location data has a long history of regulatory action and public concern because precise trails can reveal home, work, health visits and religious or political activity. Provenance matters, so buyers ask for the chain of custody from app to SDK to broker to reseller. Contracts in this market commonly cover permitted use, downstream restrictions, deletion and audit, and this page does not give legal advice. The site's compliance and regulation pages, 219 in total, show how much of this work now sits with legal and privacy teams.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction is toward less granular, more regulated and more on-device processing. Differential privacy, synthetic data and federated learning are being tested to reduce the need to move raw trails. Regulators are pushing for clearer consent and stronger deletion rights, which may shrink some panels and raise the value of compliant sources. Buyers are asking for provenance metadata and independent audits as standard. The field will likely keep converging with retail analytics, urban planning and public health research, with tighter controls on what can be sold.
